results.text:
What box office numbers for 2025 tell us about the state of movie theaters

Jan 2, 2026 - Business

# The 2025 box office comeback that wasn't

- Sara Fischer,
- Kerry Flynn

Add Axios on Google

Add Axios as your preferred source to

see more of our stories on Google.

Add Axios on Google

Data: Box Office Mojo; Chart: Axios Visuals

The 2025 North American box office fell short of the $9 billion analysts projected heading into the year, thanks to underperforming sequels and superhero movies that led to an especially weak summer and fall season.

Why it matters: Domestic entertainment tends to do well amid inflation and economic uncertainty, as people pull back from pricier international travel. But while concerts and theme parks boomed in the U.S. this year, theaters struggled — signaling the box office business faces unique challenges.

By the numbers: The domestic box office brought in roughly $8.6 billion last year, slightly above 2024's haul but down 3% from 2023 and down significantly (27% and 24%) from pre-pandemic highs of $11.9 billion and $11.4 billion in 2018 and 2019, respectively.

- As was the case in 2024, PG-rated films dominated ticket sales, with family-friendly animation attracting larger group sales compared to dramas, horror and gorier action films.
- 2025's top performer domestically was " A Minecraft Movie," setting records in April as the biggest box office debut for a video game adaptation.
- Disney's " Zootopia 2," which released around Thanksgiving, saw the highest global animated box office opening of all time and the biggest global debut of 2025. It is now Disney Animation's highest grossing movie ever, having crossed $1.46 billion at the global box office.

Data: Comscore; Chart: Axios Visuals

Between the lines: Despite a few hits like "Lilo & Stitch" and "Superman," a sluggish summer and fall dragged down overall results.

- The domestic summer box office, which extends from May to Labor Day, brought in roughly $3.67 billion in sales this year, per Comscore, marking one of the worst summer showings in decades — excluding the pandemic.

Yes, but: IMAX is up, on track for its biggest year yet with $1.2 billion revenue from hits like "Avatar: Fire and Ash" and "Ne Zha 2."

- "A lot of the movies were filmed for IMAX this year," IMAX CEO Rich Gelfond said at Media Trends Live, noting the "fantastic" slate included "F1," "Mission Impossible" and "Sinners.
- Gelfond added that IMAX has been gaining market share post-pandemic as moviegoers seek more premium experiences.

Zoom out: The weaker overall turnout, combined with ongoing studio consolidation, has Hollywood heavyweights worried about the future of domestic film production.

- Actors and unions have spoken out against a pending sale of Warner Bros. Discovery's studio and streaming assets to Netflix, arguing consolidation would mean fewer distribution options for creators and the death of theaters.
- Netflix executives say they will keep releasing Warner Bros. films in theaters if a deal goes through. But the theater industry is skeptical that traditional theatrical windows will survive long term, which the box office relies on.

What to watch: President Trump has twice threatened to impose a 100% tariff on foreign-made movies this year. But Hollywood lobbyists say the threat feels empty, as historically services have been impossible to tax.

- Still, policymakers have responded to Trump's tariff threat with some positive momentum for movie producers. California Gov. Gavin Newsom passed a major expansion of the state's film and television tax credit program to help preserve jobs.

Zootopia 2 Is 2025's Highest-Grossing Domestic Release Over Minecraft Zootopia 2 Is 2025's Highest-Grossing Domestic Release Over Minecraft

“ Zootopia 2” has cemented yet another box office benchmark, surpassing “A Minecraft Movie” to stand as the highest-grossing domestic release of 2025.

Disney‘s animated sequel, which has been a theatrical juggernaut since Thanksgiving, had notched just about every other one of the year’s box office records, including Hollywood’s biggest earner internationally ($1.425 billion) and worldwide ($1.85 billion). However, “A Minecraft Movie” loomed larger in North America with $424.08 million. Now, after 13 weekends in the top 10 on domestic charts, “Zootopia 2” has officially pulled a hair ahead with $424.2 million in North America.

## Related Stories

### ‘72 Hours' Review: Kevin Hart Tries to Be Down With the Kids in a Mediocre 'Hangover' Knockoff

Last year marked Disney’s biggest year on record since pre-pandemic times, with “Zootopia 2,” as well as two other billion-dollar behemoths, “Lilo & Stitch” and “Avatar: Fire and Ash,” helping to propel ticket sales past $6 billion globally.

### Popular on Variety

Released nine years after original, “Zootopia 2” hit theaters ahead of Thanksgiving with$158 million in North America and $559 million worldwide over the five-day holiday weekend. Those revenues ranked as the second largest Thanksgiving launch, the best start ever for an animated film, as well as the fourth-biggest worldwide debut in box office history (following “Avengers: Endgame,” “Avengers: Infinity War” and “Spider-Man: No Way Home”).

Buoyed by great reviews and stellar word-of-mouth, the family film soon became the fastest PG release ever to reach $1 billion worldwide, crossing the milestone in 17 days. It has since surpassed “Inside Out 2” to become Hollywood’s highest-grossing animated film of all time, and it overtook “Avengers: Endgame” as the biggest Motion Picture Association (MPA) title ever in China. On all-time charts, “Zootopia 2” is currently the eighth-biggest film in box office history.

Jared Bush and Byron Howard directed “Zootopia 2,” which takes place in a metropolis inhabited by animals and follows a rabbit police officer (Ginnifer Goodwin) and con artist fox (Jason Bateman) as they reunite to pursue a mysterious new reptilian resident (Ke Huy Quan). Given the never-ending box office accolades, it’s only a matter of time before Disney announces the inevitable “Zootopia 3.”

List of highest-grossing films in the United States by year

Steven Spielberg has directed a record four films to end the year as the highest-grossing in the U.S.

This is a listing of the highest-grossing films by year, based on their United States box-office gross. The films are listed by in-year release, rather than the gross they accumulated during a calendar year.

Six directors have directed the highest-grossing film on multiple occasions: George Lucas, Steven Spielberg, James Cameron, Sam Raimi, Robert Zemeckis, and Chris Columbus. Spielberg has the record, directing four of the yearly highest-grossing films: Raiders of the Lost Ark(1981), E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial(1982), Jurassic Park(1993), and Saving Private Ryan(1998). Lucas has directed three such films, all of which are part of the Star Wars franchise, which he created: the original Star Wars(1977), and two of its prequels The Phantom Menace(1999), and Revenge of the Sith(2005). James Cameron has also directed three such films: Terminator 2: Judgment Day(1991), Titanic(1997), and Avatar(2009). Sam Raimi, Robert Zemeckis, and Chris Columbus have directed two each: Spider-Man(2002) and Spider-Man 3(2007) for Raimi; Back to the Future(1985) and Forrest Gump(1994) for Zemeckis; Home Alone(1990) and Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone(2001) for Columbus.

Films that are a part of larger film or media franchises are frequently atop the highest-grossing films in the United States. The Star Wars franchise has had the highest-grossing film in eight years since 1977. In addition to the aforementioned three which Lucas directed, the franchise also had The Force Awakens, Rogue One, and The Last Jedi finish as the highest-grossing in 2015, 2016, and 2017, respectively. The Marvel Cinematic Universe has had four films atop the yearly U.S. box office: The Avengers(2012), Black Panther(2018), Avengers: Endgame(2019), and Spider-Man: No Way Home(2021). No Way Home also gave the Spider-Man film franchise its third leading film. Batman films, Harry Potter, Top Gun, and Toy Story are the other franchises with two films to top the U.S. box office in a single year.

# Weekend predictions: $300 million or more on cards for Spider-Man after monster $72 million from previews

July 31, 2026

Spider-Man: Brand New Day set out on its theatrical journey on Wednesday, with special screenings on that day followed by preview shows yesterday. The movie has already earned a monster $72 million over two days, giving it the biggest preview total of all time, ahead of Avengers: Endgame, which earned $60 million on April 25, 2019 on its way to the best weeekend of all time for a movie at the box office: $357 million.

The question going into this weekend is whether Brand New Day can beat that number. While no-one can say for sure right now, it is a possibility, and $300 million is looking like a good bet.

Here’s our model’s take on the situation.

Brand New Day has been tracking very well for a long time, and our model has had it favorite to be the top earner of 2026 for several months. Tracking over the past few weeks had increased the model’s prediction to forecast an opening well over $200 million…

The preview numbers point to something well over $300 million…

Whether Brand New Day can hit $350 million or more will depend heavily on factors such as word of mouth, repeat viewings, and the continued showing of The Odyssey in IMAX and other premium screens. Note that the Wednesday special screenings do factor into our prediction, but don’t have a huge impact. The timing of the previews on Thursday are not factored into the prediction, and could have a bearing on the final result. Endgame’s previews started at 6pm, while Brand New Day was playing from noon. That’s cause for a little caution on the prediction, and is reflected in the final predicted opening of $323 million.

---

Here’s the model’s take on the top 10:

The Odyssey faces its first major test this weekend, and could drop more steeply than the model expects. There is a possibility it will benefit from walk-up moviegoers who can’t find a seat to see Spider-Man.

As usual, we’ll post numbers as soon as we receive them through the weekend, and, if you need a head start on the numbers for upcoming movies, The Numbers Business Report has predictions and tracking for all movies coming up in the next 12 months, and our weekly subscription option puts you first in line for our last-minute weekend predictions.

# Theater counts: Spider‑Man swings into 4,487 theaters to kick off its run

July 30, 2026

Once again, last weekend’s box office was ruled by Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, which powered to an epic $90.02 million in its sophomore frame to lift its domestic tally to $289.39 million. It is firmly entrenched at the top of the charts with a haul of $334 million, but the marketplace is poised for another jolt as Spider-Man: Brand New Day readies its launch across 4,487 theaters this weekend.

The newest chapter in the Spider‑Man franchise picks up four years after the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home, with Peter now an adult living in total isolation after choosing to erase himself from the lives and memories of those he loves. Crime‑fighting in a New York that no longer knows his name, he’s become a full‑time guardian of the city, but as the strain of that responsibility mounts, a startling physical evolution begins to take hold, threatening his very existence. Meanwhile, a strange pattern of crimes signals the rise of one of the most formidable threats he’s ever faced. Tom Holland returns as the Wall‑Crawler, joined once again by Zendaya as MJ. Debuting in a massive 4,487 theaters, the film lands as the 13th widest release of all time, slotted between the 4,476‑theater launch of 2019’s Aladdin, and the 4,529 theater start by Despicable Me 3 back in 2017. The debut also marks the largest opening footprint since 2024, when Beetlejuice Beetlejuice arrived in 4,575 locations.

One other film opening in wide release this weekend is I Want Your Sex. Beginning its run in 708 cinemas, the comedy‑thriller follows Elliot, who lands an exciting job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy. His fantasies quickly blur into reality when Erika taps him as her sexual muse, pulling him into a world of obsession, power, betrayal, and murder that proves far deeper than he ever imagined. Olivia Wilde and Cooper Hoffman star in the Gregg Araki–directed feature, which will play in 660 U.S. locations and 48 venues across Canada.

Rounding out the top five widest films this weekend is our current chart topper, with The Odyssey shedding 82 locations, settling in with 3,860 locations. Moana dips below the 4,000 mark, easing to 3,010 movie houses, while Minions & Monsters and Toy Story 5 complete the list with 3,014 and 3,035 theaters, respectively.

Looking ahead to next weekend, three wide releases enter the marketplace: Eli Roth’s horror entry Ice Cream Man; Super Troopers 3; and the romantic-comedy, One Night Only. The latter two are slated to launch in approximately 2,700 and 3,000 theaters, respectively.

# Weekend projections: Fantastic hold for The Odyssey sets up monster run

July 26, 2026

The Odyssey is enjoying at fantastic hold this weekend, with Universal projecting a second weekend of $87 million domestically, a drop of only 30% from its huge $123.5-million opening. The studio reports an even more remarkable 10% decline in holdover international markets, with the film now standing at $353.26 million internationally, and $639.632 million worldwide.

Here are the official studio projections for the weekend (click the image for a full chart of all films reporting so far).

Two records Universal is touting this morning are that The Odyssey will have the second-best second weekend for an R-rated film, behind only Deadpool & Wolverine, and it’ll have the third-best hold for a movie that opened to over $100 million, behind Wicked(a Thanksgiving-boosted 28%) and Top Gun: Maverick(29%, despite coming off a Memorial Day Weekend opening).

Our model predicts it will finish with $461 million domestically as of this morning, but with a huge potential upside: anything up to $750 million is still on the cards, per the model, and something over $500 million a pretty good bet. By way of comparison, the model predicts Toy Story 5 will end with $477 million, with an upper bound of $570 million. Right now, my money would be on The Odyssey being the top grosser between those two (although Spider-Man: Brand New Day will probably top them both).

The Odyssey is ranking No. 1 in nearly every major international territory and running ahead of Oppenheimer and The Dark Knight Rises at the same point in most of them. The UK and Ireland leads the way with $14.9 million, down just 11% from opening weekend for a $46.3-million cume that has already passed the lifetime totals of Interstellar and Tenet. France added $12.3 million for a $31.8-million total, making the film the fourth-biggest release of the year there, while Italy posted $10.5 million—the biggest second weekend ever for a Hollywood film in the market—to reach $28.9 million and rank as the year’s third-biggest film. Germany contributed $7.8 million on a 7% drop for a $20.5-million cume, and Spain reached $15.5 million, passing The Dark Knight Rises to become Christopher Nolan’s third-biggest film there. Holds were similarly strong elsewhere. Australia eased 16% to $7.9 million for a $20.7-million total, Mexico slipped just 2% to $7.5 million and a $19-million cume, and Brazil rose 6% from its opening to $4.6 million, reaching $11.1 million. India took in $3.6 million for a $14.4-million total, making The Odyssey the biggest MPA release of the year there and Nolan’s second-biggest film ever in the market. The Netherlands held flat at $2.9 million to reach $7.7 million, and Saudi Arabia rose 3% to $2.7 million for a $7.2-million cume, in line with Oppenheimer’s pace. Additional markets posting minimal declines or gains included the U.A.E. (-11%), Denmark (+8%), Colombia (+12%), Argentina (+72%), Turkey (-6%), and Belgium (-9%). Across these territories, the film has now surpassed the lifetime grosses of Interstellar, Dunkirk, and Tenet in many markets, with IMAX accounting for a notable share of business—21% of the gross to date in the UK and Ireland.

Bruce Nash, bruce.nash@the-numbers.com.

# Weekend predictions: Second weekend benchmark for The Odyssey is $70 million

July 24, 2026

There’s no question The Odyssey will dominate movie theaters again this weekend, with continued soldout shows in IMAX and other PLF theaters, and enough buzz to keep regular screens busy. With seven days’ data now available, our model has been crunching the numbers to produce a prediction for the movie’s second weekend. As of this morning, it thinks $69.5 million is the target.

Other rumors suggest something more like $80 million, while a “typical” second weekend would come in closer to $50 million. The best benchmark comp is probably Oppenheimer, which fell 43% in its second weekend. A similar decline would give The Odyssey just over $70 million this weekend.

What we can say for sure is that it’s had an excellent start, with just short of $200 million domestically in its first seven days. The model thinks a total around $500 million is on the cards, with a chance it will briefly be the top-grossing movie of the year. # Theater counts: Moana still reigns as widest release as The Odyssey soars

As no surprise, the weekend box office was dominated by Christopher Nolan’s action-epic The Odyssey, which stormed to a career‑best opening for the director with $123.5 million from 3,919 theaters, buoyed by a commanding IMAX presence across North America. Despite three new wide releases entering the fray this weekend, The Odyssey wiil maintain its lead heading into its second go-round.

Landing in 1,944 theaters this weekend is Hadestown: The Musical. It is a live theater capture of the hit musical Hadestown, which won eight Tony Awards in 2019, including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album, featuring the five original principals of the Broadway company. The film is described as a genre-defying new musical which blends modern American folk music with New Orleans-inspired jazz to reimagine a sweeping ancient tale.

Hitting 1,600 theaters this weekend is Alan Ritchson’s gritty action vehicle Motor City. Set against a 1970s Detroit backdrop, the story centers on a blue‑collar romantic who’s framed by a brutal gangster after falling for his girlfriend. After serving a long stretch behind bars, he comes back with one goal in mind: payback. The film features Ben Foster, Pablo Schreiber, Lionel Boyce, and Shailene Woodley.

Another of the fresh faces entering theaters this weekend is Her Private Hell. Set in a futuristic metropolis, the film follows Sophie Thatcher as a troubled young woman searching for her father after a mysterious mist unleashes a deadly, elusive entity. Her path intersects with an American GI on his own harrowing mission to rescue his daughter from the depths of hell, pulling both characters into a collision of survival and fate. The film is set to roll out across 670 theaters.

The top five widest releases conclude with Moana still the only film over 4,000 theaters, playing in 4,015 this weekend. Finally, Evil Dead Burn occupies the fifth widest spot, showing in 2,385 venues.

# Weekend projections: The Odyssey surges to $124.5-million debut. Here are all the stats

July 19, 2026

Despite a suspicion that some moviegoers are holding off to see it from a good seat in a premium format theater, The Odyssey is heading for a stellar $124.5-million opening weekend, according to Universal’s Sunday-morning projection. That tops our Friday-morning prediction by a few million dollars, and is comfortably ahead of our pre-release forecast of $106 million.

Its opening is the third-best of Christopher Nolan’s career in North America, behind the $158.4 million earned by The Dark Knight, and The Dark Knight Rises’ $160.9 million. Universal says this is Nolan’s biggest global opening of all time, with $139.564 million internationally, and a total of $264.064 worldwide expected by close of business on Sunday.

Here are the official studio projections for the weekend (click the image for a full chart of all films reporting so far).

The Odyssey opened to an audience that skewed modestly male, with men representing 59% of ticket buyers. The film drew heavily from older moviegoers, with 76% of the audience aged 25 and over. At the same time, younger adults were well represented, with 18–34-year-olds accounting for half of the total audience. Within that group, 25–34-year-olds made up the largest segment at 30%, followed by 18–24 at 20%. Older cohorts were distributed across 35–44 (19%), 45–54 (12%), and 55+ (15%), while teens aged 13–17 accounted for a small share at 4%.

The audience composition by ethnicity showed a broad mix, led by Caucasian moviegoers at 50%. Hispanic audiences represented 22%, followed by Black moviegoers at 12% and Asian audiences at 9%, with Native American and other groups comprising 6%.

Premium and large-format screens accounted for a substantial portion of the film’s opening weekend revenue. Enhanced formats overall delivered 53% of the domestic gross. IMAX screenings contributed a combined 24%, split between 20% from digital locations and 4% from 70mm presentations. Additional large-format options included non-Dolby premium large formats at 20%, while traditional film formats such as 70mm and 35mm accounted for 3% and 0.3%, respectively. Dolby Cinema represented 4% of the total, with no measurable contribution from 3D formats.

Bruce Nash, bruce.nash@the-numbers.com.

# Weekend predictions: The Odyssey eyeing $120-million opening

July 17, 2026

The Odyssey posted the best previews of 2026 so far on Thursday, with its $17.6-million haul just overtaking Toy Story 5’s $17.5 million. That puts it on track to deliver Christopher Nolan’s best non-franchise opening weekend ever, although a 2026 opening-weekend record looks unlikely.

Here are our model’s predictions for The Odyssey, beginning with our baseline analysis.

# The Numbers Business Report asks, where have all the indie films gone?

June 11, 2026

Movies from the major studios may get most of the buzz, but by the raw numbers, most movies that get made and distributed have more humble origins. In the latest The Numbers Business Report, we look at the universe of movies produced and distributed for sale, either in theaters, on a digital transactional platform, or a subscription streaming service in the domestic market (the United States and Canada) between 2021 and 2025. In this study, we call these “commercial releases,” in contrast to “ad-supported content,” which includes content produced for platforms like YouTube, and also movies released solely on AVOD services.

What we’ve found is a tale of two markets. On the one hand, the theatrical market has shown growth over the past five years, with 101 domestically-produced and released narrative features earning over $1 million at the box office in 2021, and 160 such movies in 2025. With new distribution technologies making it easier than ever to get movies into theaters, the total number of domestically-produced narrative features getting any sort of theatrical release has also increased, from 494 in 2021 to 598 in 2025.

The increase in that number contrasts with a steep decline among direct-to-digital titles. Movies bypassing theaters, but still having a commercial release, fell from 1,427 in 2022 to 721 last year. That’s a decline of nearly 50% in just three years.

Disney dominated 2025 box office. Can it keep the crown in 2026?
results.author: Sarah Whitten
results.text:
Disney dominated 2025 box office. Can it keep the crown in 2026?

Key Points

- Box office ticket sales in the United States and Canada rose about 4% in 2025 to $9.05 billion.
- Disney accounted for the highest share of that haul with $2.49 billion in ticket sales, or 27.5%.
- The studio’s standout performance came on the backs of already popular intellectual property like “Lilo & Stitch,” “Zootopia,” the Marvel Cinematic Universe and “Avatar.”

Courtesy of Disney Enterprises Inc.

Blue aliens, a family of superheroes and a city of talking animals boosted the Walt Disney Company to the top of the domestic box office in 2025.

Full-year ticket sales in the United States and Canada rose about 4% from 2024 to $9.05 billion. Disney accounted for the highest share of that haul with $2.49 billion in ticket sales, or 27.5%, according to data from Comscore.

It’s closest competitors were Warner Bros. Discovery, which tallied $1.9 billion domestically, or 21%, and Universal, which took in $1.7 billion, or 19.7%. Together, these three studios accounted for nearly 70% of the domestic box office market share.

No other studio surpassed $1 billion in domestic ticket sales or accounted for more than 7% of the total box office haul.

″[Warner Bros., Disney and Universal] have the advantage of having at least two or more distinct and successful sub-brands labels — such as Marvel under Disney, New Line under WB and Illumination under Universal — under their corporate umbrella that enables these studios to dominate at least in terms of the overall box office and percentage of the marketplace that they control,” said Paul Dergarabedian, head of marketplace trends at Comscore.

Disney’s standout performance came on the backs of already popular intellectual property. Four of its films were part of the top 10 highest-grossing domestic releases of the year, including the live-action remake of “Lilo & Stitch,” a sequel to 2016′s “Zootopia,” another entrant in the Marvel Cinematic Universe with “Fantastic Four: First Steps” and a third “Avatar” film.

“Most years at the box office are dominated by known IP and non-original content; films that have the baked in brand name recognition that theoretically gives those films a leg up in terms of marketing and potential box office success,” Dergarabedian said.

In fact, nine of the 10 biggest movies at the domestic box offices were from existing IP. Warner Bros.′ “Sinners” was the only original title to make the list.

“In 2025 there were some big budget originals that did incredibly well ... but lest anyone think that trend is going away, 2026 looks to eclipse 2025 in terms of the number of high-profile sequels and known IP on the slate for the year,” Dergarabedian said.

That’s especially true for Disney.

The studio is set to release its first Star Wars film in theaters since 2019 called “The Mandalorian and Grogu” after the popular characters of its “The Mandalorian” series on Disney+; “Toy Story 5” is will hit theaters in June followed by a live-action “Moana” in July; then the hotly anticipated “Avengers: Doomsday” arrives in December.

A new Spider-Man film will also sling into theaters in 2026, but as part of a deal with Sony to have the character as part of Disney’s MCU, Sony keeps the majority of box office profits while Disney gets merchandise sales.

The box office will also get a boost from Warner Bros.′ “Supergirl” and “Dune: Part Three,” Universal’s “Minions 3,” “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” and “The Odyssey,” Lionsgate’s “Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” and Sony’s third “Jumanji” film.

“As we look into 2026, there’s plenty of optimism to go around,” said Shawn Robbins, director of analytics at Fandango and founder of Box Office Theory “The slate is packed with top-tier franchises, some fan-driven and others family-oriented, alongside filmmaker-driven tentpoles ... plus an inevitable crop of strong or potentially surprising performers out of horror, comedy, indie, and other genres.”
